submission.justification:
Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 36 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.875% at the allocated trigger rate of 8 kHz. This represents a significant improvement over the baseline configuration tested in 2025 (35 GeV, 92% efficiency).

Through systematic threshold optimization, I evaluated all three candidate algorithms across the allowed threshold range (20-60 GeV):

- Algorithm-L1 peaks at 36 GeV with 93.875% efficiency
- Algorithm-L2 peaks at 35 GeV with 86.035% efficiency  
- Algorithm-L3 peaks at 30 GeV with 73.941% efficiency

Algorithm-L1's iterative topological clustering with learned calibration significantly outperforms the other candidates, providing 7.8 percentage points higher efficiency than Algorithm-L2 and nearly 20 percentage points higher than Algorithm-L3. The optimal threshold of 36 GeV balances signal acceptance against background rejection to maximize efficiency at the allocated rate.

All candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs), so Algorithm-L1 is fully deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware. The 36 GeV threshold falls well within the allowed range of 20-60 GeV.
